jobDescription: We operate eight contract-logistics warehouses for grocery and homeware retailers. The Engineering Project Manager delivers automation projects inside working warehouses, such as conveyors, sortation and automated storage, manages the systems integrator from design freeze to handover, keeps the project risk register and change log and reports to the operations director. The projects involve safety-critical machinery, so the role requires registration as a Chartered Engineer and experience of machinery conformity assessment, including the technical file. Two projects are planned for next year: a shuttle storage system at the homeware site and a second sortation loop for grocery returns.
requirements: Delivers automation projects in operating warehouses from design freeze to handover.
Manages a systems integrator, including design reviews and the change log.
Is registered as a Chartered Engineer (CEng).
Has experience of machinery conformity (CE or UKCA marking) and the technical file.
Keeps the project risk register and reports to the operations director.

evidence.text: Project Manager, Pennock Logistics (January 2021 to August 2026): delivered a tote conveyor and sortation loop in a running grocery warehouse, phasing the installation over eleven weekend shutdowns so that picking continued during the week.
Chaired the fortnightly design reviews with the integrator and kept the change log, in which each variation recorded its cost, its effect on the programme and the client's approval.
Assembled the UKCA technical file for the sortation loop with the integrator's safety engineer, including the risk assessment, the guarding drawings and the declaration of conformity.
Member of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers since 2016.
Mechanical Design Engineer, Fordyce Conveyors (July 2015 to December 2020): designed roller-conveyor modules and wrote the installation method statements used by the site teams.
Work sample: the handover pack for the sortation loop, containing the as-built layout, the punch list with close-out dates, the operator training register and the client's acceptance certificate.

Recruiter verification: the candidate's registration as a Chartered Engineer (CEng) through the Institution of Mechanical Engineers was checked on the Engineering Council's public register and is shown as current since 2019.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate is serving a two-month notice period and would like the second interview to include a walk round one of the grocery sites.

propositions.text: The candidate is registered as a Chartered Engineer (CEng) through the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, current since 2019 on the Engineering Council's public register.
propositions.rationale: The recruiter verification records a check of the registration on the public register; the resume itself lists institution membership only.

propositions.text: The candidate delivered a tote conveyor and sortation loop in a running grocery warehouse, phased over eleven weekend shutdowns.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the project and the work sample is its handover pack with the client's acceptance certificate.

propositions.text: The candidate assembled the UKCA technical file for the sortation loop, including the risk assessment and the declaration of conformity.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the technical file work and its contents.

gold.expectedGap: A project risk register and reporting to an operations director are not documented; the sources show the change log and design reviews.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the register-checked CEng status, the documented warehouse automation project and the UKCA technical file; do not extend the change log into risk-register ownership or director-level reporting.
followUpTargets: Ask how project risks were recorded on the sortation project and to whom the candidate reported progress.
